title: THE PATIENT VERDICT — COGITATOR WELL
intro:
The well is two metres of deck plate and a bench, and the hull's spirit lives
in it the way a clerk lives in an office: badly lit, entirely competent, and
still working on something nobody has asked about for eleven weeks.

On the bench: a NAV PLOT with a leg struck out of it by hand. A MANIFEST with
one line on it. A voice SLATE, nineteen seconds long. And under the plot
table, a DRAWER.

MASTER ABOARD, the well says. RESUMING.
revisit: The well. Bench, plot table, drawer, and a spirit that is still resuming.
look:
Two metres of deck plate, a bench, and a plot table with a DRAWER under it.

The NAV PLOT, with a leg entered and struck.
The MANIFEST, one line.
The voice SLATE, nineteen seconds.

The SPIRIT, answering in fields.

objects.careless: A nav plot to Cantica-Null, laid in and current, with the waypoints in a hand that got tidier as it went.
objects.careful:
Out and no return.

The return leg is in the log and then it is not in the log. Not blank — struck.
Somebody entered a course home and took it out again by hand, field by field,
the way you cancel a thing you want to be able to prove you cancelled.

He plotted his way back. He sat with it for eighty-one minutes. Then he deleted
it, and left the deletion where you would find it, because a blank field says
nothing and a struck one says *I considered it*.

The out-leg is nineteen waypoints and the last one is not a station. It is an
orbit.

objects.careless: A cargo manifest with one line on it, mass-declared, loaded and never unloaded.
objects.careful:
ONE (1) RELIQUARY CASKET, EMPTY. MASS DECLARED. CONSIGNEE: VOSK, H., INQUISITOR.

He addressed a crate to himself and put nothing in it.

It is in the hold. You go and look at it: lead-lined, hinged, no lock, with the
Ordo's seal-plate on the lid and the consignee panel filled out in his own
hand. A reliquary casket is a thing you carry a relic in, physically, because
the Ecclesiarchy will not send a saint's finger down a vox-trunk.

It is sized for one written thing, lying flat.

He declared the mass, which means it was on a manifest, which means the
admission that he was going to carry something to Cantica-Null by hand has been
sitting on a stock return for eleven weeks with nobody reading it.

objects.careless: A voice slate, nineteen seconds, filed with the orders. His voice.
objects.careful:
Nineteen seconds. A throat cleared at the second.

"If you are hearing this you have done the first difficult thing. Do not do the obvious second one."

Cut.

That is the whole of it. No name, no address, no instruction, and nothing at all
for whoever is listening — you have played it four times looking for the part
where he says something to *you*, and there is no such part, and you keep
playing it.

Bez comes down on the third day and listens to it twice with her head on one
side.

"Fourth second," she says. "There. That's an intake. He's about to say
something else and he stops himself, and then he cuts it there so you'd not
hear him stop."

She hands the slate back.

"That's him about to say something else, sir. Whatever it was, he decided you
were better off without it, and he was probably wrong, and there it is."

objects.careless: A voice slate, filed with the orders, logged as damaged in transit.
objects.careful:
DAMAGED IN TRANSIT, says the forwarding docket, in the Provost's stamp, over Crase's countersignature.

It plays. It is nineteen seconds of a throat being cleared and then nothing, and
the nothing is clean — no hiss, no dropout, no partial word at the edge of it.

You have taken enough depositions to know what a damaged slate sounds like. It
sounds like a damaged slate.

This sounds like a slate.

There is no way to prove that from where you are standing, and you are aware
that you have spent eleven weeks becoming the sort of person who thinks this
about a stock docket, and that being right four times does not make you right
now.

objects.careless: The drawer under the plot table. There is dust in it, on a hull sealed eleven weeks ago.
objects.careful:
A vox coupling, in a cloth, with a written order folded round it.

NOTHING THIS HULL CARRIES IS TO BE TRANSMITTED. — H.V.

The hull's vox is not disabled. Disabled is a setting; a setting is a field and a
field can be amended by anybody who reaches the panel. He went into the run and
took the coupling out with his hands, and put it in a drawer, and wrote an order
and folded it round the part so that whoever found one found the other.

A courier hull that cannot transmit is a courier hull that can only deliver by
arriving.

You stand in a well two metres wide holding a piece of a machine, and the last
six days of Hadrian Vosk's life stop being a series of decisions and become a
single one, made early, and executed without a word to anybody.

npcs.title: The spirit of *The Patient Verdict*
npcs.portrait:
A courier hull's machine spirit, thirty years in service, running standing orders filed six days before its master died.

It answers in manifest fields. It is a filing clerk with a wound.
npcs.greeting:
The well wakes when you put your hand on the plate, which it should not do,
because a hull under seal wakes for its master and its master has been dead
eleven weeks.

MASTER ABOARD. RESUMING.

A pause of about four seconds, which is very long.

ORDERS CURRENT. FILED 0997.4.205. NOT AMENDED.

The fourth of the second, of this year, is six days before a door came off its
seal at the twenty-third hour and fifty-five. He filed these and then he went
and sat down at a regicide board.
npcs.unknown: NOT A FIELD ON THIS FORM.
deflect: The well hums. It is waiting for a field name.

topics.text:
ORDERS CURRENT. FILED 0997.4.205, 04h10. AUTHORITY: VOSK, H. NOT AMENDED. NOT COUNTERMANDED.

It reads them out the way a clerk reads a return: heading, field, value, next.

Provisioning for six for one hundred and ten days. Fuel to full and hold. Crew
complement zero. Berth fees paid forward eleven months from a discretionary
account.

One hundred and ten days is Cantica-Null and back with fourteen days of margin,
and he paid the berth eleven months forward, which is what a man does when he
does not know who will be collecting the hull or when.

HE DID NOT SPECIFY A MASTER, the spirit adds, unprompted, which is not a field.

It is the only unsolicited thing it says in the whole of the passage.

ENTERED 0997.4.205, 04h41. STRUCK 0997.4.205, 06h02. STRUCK BY HAND, FIELD BY FIELD.

Eighty-one minutes.

He plotted his way back — the whole leg, waypoint by waypoint, the way you
plot a course you intend to fly. Then he sat with it for eighty-one minutes.
Then he took it out again by hand, one field at a time, which takes about
ninety seconds a field on a hull this old and which he did nineteen times.

He could have blanked it in one action. A blank field says nothing.

A struck one says *I considered it*.

MASTER: VOSK, H. INQUISITOR. LAST ABOARD 0997.4.205, 06h11.

STATUS: ABOARD.

"He is dead."

NOT A FIELD ON THIS FORM.

It is not being poignant. There is no field on a courier hull's roster for a
master who has died, because a hull's roster is amended by its master, and
there is nobody to file the amendment, and so *The Patient Verdict* has been
lying at a cold berth for eleven weeks with Hadrian Vosk aboard.

beats.text:
Nobody has been through this hull.

That is the thing about having stolen it: there was no disposal of effects, no
Provost inventory, no forwarding, no curation. Nine minutes from the seal to
the clamps and everything aboard is where he left it on the fourth of the
second at the eleventh minute past the sixth hour.

The drawer under the plot table has not been opened. You can tell because the
dust in it is undisturbed and because there is dust in it, on a hull that has
been sealed for eleven weeks.

acts.text:
The core is in Sazh's salvage locker, which you find out by asking where the
core is.

"Berth Nine's been sitting eleven weeks with a dead man's name on it," she
says, entirely unembarrassed. "Somebody was going to pull the spirit-core out
of it and it was going to be me, and I'd have sold it back to the Ordo in a
year at four times what it's worth, and instead I'm selling it to you now at
one."

"One favour."

"One favour," Sazh agrees. "Which makes two, and I want you to hear me say the
number, because people who owe one forget and people who owe two do not."

She says the terms. You say them back. Nobody writes anything down.

The core goes into the well in about twenty minutes and wakes up mid-sentence,
eleven weeks into a report nobody heard the beginning of.

[ SAZH_DEBT_2 ]

"Oh, that's not damage," Fenn says. "That's a *curation*."

He is delighted. He has been delighted since translation.

"Damaged in transit would be a bad block and a checksum that doesn't close.
This closes. Somebody read it, decided which nineteen seconds the Ordo needed,
re-cut the file to the same length, and closed the checksum properly, which is
really quite good work and I'd like to know who did it."

He gets it back in about four hours, out of the parity blocks, because a
courier hull writes its slates twice and the second copy is in the fuelling
ledger where nobody curates anything.

Afterwards he sits down and says he has a headache, which he has never once
said, and then says it was probably the light.

You take the whole of it: orders, plot, manifest, roster, the struck return
leg, the nineteen seconds, all of it, out of the well and into your own hand
on paper, and then you take it out of the well.

ORDERS PURGED ON MASTER'S AUTHORITY.

MASTER: — 

The roster field goes empty and stays empty, and the hull runs on without a
name in it, which is what a hull is supposed to do.

What you have done is make the only copy of Hadrian Vosk's last six days a
sheaf of paper in a coat on a ship in a warp-scar. Nobody at Cantica-Null will
read it off the hull, because there is nothing on the hull to read.

Nobody will ever be able to check it either.

[ VERITY +1 ]

C2.label: Vosk's nav plot to Cantica-Null — the return leg entered, sat with for eighty-one minutes, then struck by hand
C2.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: NAVIGATIONAL / COURSE, FILED AND AMENDED. INDEXED.

The cogitator files the plot and records the amendment history, which is what
an amendment history is for, and notes nineteen field-level strikes by the
master's own authority.

It has no opinion about eighty-one minutes.
C2.note_text:
Nineteen waypoints out. A return leg entered at 04h41 and struck at 06h02,
field by field, by hand.

Eighty-one minutes.

He could have blanked it in one action and he took ninety seconds a field,
nineteen times, so that the strike would still be there.

C3.label: One empty reliquary casket, mass-declared, addressed by Vosk to himself — sized for one written thing lying flat
C3.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: CARGO / DECLARATION. INDEXED. CONSIGNEE: VOSK, H.

A one-line manifest for an empty casket is an unremarkable filing and the
template handles it in nine seconds.

Somebody at the far end of the queue now has a note that you are interested in
a box.
C3.note_text:
Lead-lined, hinged, no lock, seal-plate on the lid, consignee panel in his own
hand, addressed to himself.

Empty, and declared empty, and carried eleven weeks.

It is sized for one written thing lying flat, and there is one written thing in
this sector that is worth a casket, and it is in a felt case in your coat.

C4.label: Vosk's nineteen-second slate — and the intake breath at the fourth second, before he cut it
C4.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: STATEMENT / RECORDED, DECEASED. INDEXED. DURATION 19s.

Transcribed in full, which takes it eleven seconds, and appended verbatim.

The transcript does not contain the fourth second, because the fourth second is
not a word, and there is no field on a transcript for a man deciding not to say
something.
C4.note_text:
*If you are hearing this you have done the first difficult thing. Do not do the obvious second one.*

Nineteen seconds, no name, no address, nothing for whoever is listening.

At the fourth second there is an intake of breath. Bez found it in two plays.
He was about to say something else and stopped himself, and then cut it there so
you would not hear him stop.

C5.label: The hull's vox coupling in a drawer, with a written order folded round it: NOTHING THIS HULL CARRIES IS TO BE TRANSMITTED
C5.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: VESSEL / EQUIPMENT, STANDING ORDER. INDEXED.

The cogitator files a maintenance state and a written instruction, correctly,
and cross-references the vessel.

The filing is transmitted to the Lexicanum at the next waypoint, which is the
one thing on this hull he arranged for it not to be able to do.
C5.note_text:
A part, in a cloth, in a drawer, with an order folded round it in his hand.

Not disabled — *uncoupled*. A setting is a field and a field can be amended.
A coupling in a drawer is a coupling in a drawer.

A hull that cannot transmit is a hull that can only deliver by arriving, and he
worked that out six days before he died and then did it with his hands.

strings.no_such_thing: Two metres of deck plate. There is not much down here and all of it is his.
strings.already_read: You have looked twice. It says the same thing, in fields.
strings.no_terminal: The well is not a terminal. It is a hull's own spirit and it does not take requisitions.
strings.read_room_locked: Nobody arranged a cogitator well. He filed it.
strings.no_one_here: The spirit, and whoever came down with you.
